response: Yes, tranexamic acid reduces desmopressin-induced hyperfibrinolysis. Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic agent that inhibits the breakdown of fibrin clots, while desmopressin can induce hyperfibrinolysis by increasing the levels of plasminogen activators. The combination of tranexamic acid with desmopressin can mitigate the risk of hyperfibrinolysis associated with desmopressin therapy.
